subject.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn

question: Should maintainers require live Discord/Codex continuation and no-duplicate proof before choosing this PR or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107388 as the canonical fix?
rationale: Both branches plausibly repair a message-delivery regression, but tests alone do not settle the user-visible continuation and duplicate-suppression behavior or which model-facing schema treatment maintainers want.

options.title: Require proof, then choose
options.body: Obtain redacted live Discord/Codex evidence for both continuation and final delivery, compare the overlapping schema changes, and retain only the stronger canonical branch.

options.title: Accept this focused patch
options.body: Treat the existing focused tests as sufficient and land this narrower runtime-only change after refreshing it against current main.

options.title: Prefer the sibling branch
options.body: Use the competing PR as canonical because it also clarifies `final` guidance, but require its own positive real behavior proof before closing this branch.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then choose
recommendation.body: Obtain redacted live Discord/Codex evidence for both continuation and final delivery, compare the overlapping schema changes, and retain only the stronger canonical branch.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected Codex terminal-recognition behavior appears to originate in their merged source-reply completion work.
